title: AtomSearch: Evidence-Grounded Tree Search for Agent Skill Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2610.19951v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent skills adapt frozen models through editable external instructions. Revising several rules at once makes changes difficult to inspect, while judging each local edit only by its immediate score can discard useful intermediate states. We introduce AtomSearch, which keeps revision actions local while using subsequent skill states to guide search. Contrastive atomic editing links each primitive rule edit to failed and successful executions, a behavioral hypothesis, and an intended scope. Skill-State Tree Search (STS) evaluates short edit compositions and selectively retains them as executable states that can be revisited and extended. Outcome memory supplies later proposals with observed repair and regression statistics. We evaluate AtomSearch across four tasks and five target models. With deepseek-v4-flash, it exceeds SkillOpt on three of four tasks, including a 9.68-percentage-point gain on LiveMathematicianBench, and SkillOpt's final

translated_title: AtomSearch：面向智能体技能优化的基于证据的树搜索
translated_abstract: 智能体技能通过可编辑的外部指令来适配冻结的模型。一次性修改多条规则会使改动难以审查，而仅凭即时得分来判断每次局部修改可能会丢弃有用的中间状态。我们提出 AtomSearch，它保持修改动作的局部性，同时利用后续的技能状态来引导搜索。对比式原子编辑将每个原始规则修改与失败和成功的执行、一个行为假设以及预期作用范围相关联。技能状态树搜索（STS）评估较短的编辑组合，并选择性地将其保留为可回访、可扩展的可执行状态。结果记忆为后续的修改提案提供已观察到的修复与回归统计数据。我们在四个任务和五个目标模型上评估了 AtomSearch。使用 deepseek-v4-flash 时，它在四个任务中的三个上超越了 SkillOpt，其中包括在 LiveMathematicianBench 上取得 9.68 个百分点的提升，以及 SkillOpt 的最终（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: AtomSearch 通过对比式原子编辑和技能状态树搜索，以证据为依据实现局部化、可回溯的智能体技能优化，在多个任务和模型上超越了 SkillOpt。
en_tdlr: AtomSearch optimizes agent skills through evidence-grounded contrastive atomic editing and skill-state tree search, enabling local, revisable improvements that outperform SkillOpt across multiple tasks and models.
